title: Balance Brackets With Locked Positions
statement:
You get a string s of ( and ) characters and a string locked of the same length made of 0 and 1.

If locked[i] is 1, the character s[i] is fixed. If it is 0, you may replace s[i] with either bracket. Return true if some choice for the free positions makes s a balanced bracket string: every ( is closed by a later ), and no ) appears before its matching (.

examples.why: Only position 1 is fixed as ")". Choose "()()" for the whole string.
Two fixed closers sit at positions 1 and 2. Only one free position comes before them, so the second ")" always closes nothing.
Scanning left to right looks fine, but the last "(" is fixed and nothing after it can close it.

hints: An odd-length string can never be balanced. For even lengths, think about what can go wrong while scanning.
Left to right, a fixed ')' needs some earlier position to act as its '('. Free positions can play that role. What is the mirror condition from the right?

Scan left to right counting free positions and fixed '(' as +1 and fixed ')' as −1; it must never go negative. Do the same from the right with the roles swapped. Even length plus both scans passing is enough.

explain.intuition:
Think about what a fixed ) needs: something before it that can be an opener. Free positions are flexible, so when scanning left to right, give every free position the benefit of the doubt and count it as an opener. If even that optimistic count goes negative, some fixed ) has nothing to close, and no choice can save it.

The same argument from the right covers fixed (: each needs something after it that can close it. If the length is even and both optimistic scans stay non-negative, a valid assignment exists. Intuitively, the free positions can be split between the two jobs without running out on either side.
steps: If the length is odd, return false.
Left to right: add 1 for a free position or a fixed (, subtract 1 for a fixed ). If the total drops below 0, return false.
Right to left: add 1 for a free position or a fixed ), subtract 1 for a fixed (. If the total drops below 0, return false.
pitfalls: Only scanning left to right. "()((" with the last two fixed passes that scan but has unclosable openers at the end.
Only checking that fixed openers and fixed closers are each at most half the length. Order matters, as in "())(".
Forgetting the odd-length check; both scans pass for "(()" with everything free.

solutions.title: Try every assignment
solutions.idea: Enumerate every choice of brackets for the free positions and test whether the result is balanced.

solutions.title: Two optimistic scans
solutions.idea: Count free positions as whatever helps. Left to right they act as openers, right to left as closers. If neither scan goes negative and the length is even, it works.

followups: Return one valid assignment instead of true/false. How do you decide which free positions become openers?
Free positions may also be deleted (become empty). Does the length check still matter?
lcTitle: Check if a Parentheses String Can Be Valid
